key_insight: A rapidly rotating cylinder in compressible flow shifts from periodic vortex shedding to multi-mode oscillatory behavior near Re≈5650, and ANN-based surrogates best capture the resulting nonlinear load dynamics.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that trained machine-learning surrogates can reduce the cost of predicting aerodynamic loads and instability onset in highly nonlinear CFD problems.
method: 101 high-fidelity simulations spanning Re = 1000–6000 were used to build the dataset.
Polynomial, Bayesian spline/RBF, and ANN surrogate models were compared for lift, drag, and instability timing.
A hierarchical refinement strategy was used to improve predictions at unseen Reynolds numbers.
evidence_signal: The database contains 101 simulations and 1 million core hours of high-fidelity CFD, with evaluation showing spline Bayesian models outperform polynomials and ANNs achieving the strongest overall predictive accuracy, especially for maximum lift and instability onset time.
watch_item: Drag prediction remains more difficult than lift, so surrogate accuracy should be checked carefully near the bifurcation and in unseen regimes.
paper_title: Supervised machine learning of compressible flow past a rotating cylinder
